column2: Whether one condition is the contrary of another depends on what it excludes at the same time, not on whether it comes after the other; so a response that presupposes a prior condition is that condition's contrary only insofar as the response consists in a state that excludes it.

When what a word names as a gift is itself an orientation of the one who receives it, the gift can be the contrary of an opposing orientation; when the gift is not an orientation, neither the gift nor merely having received it is such a contrary.
